article.headline: Claude Code Is an OS — Carl Vellotti Maps the Control Plane
article.lede: Carl Vellotti, creator of a free interactive Claude Code course for product managers, joined Aakash Gupta's Growth Podcast for a third time to walk through the advanced setup most tutorials skip. The central argument: Claude Code — Anthropic's agentic coding CLI — is best understood not as a sophisticated autocomplete but as an extensible operating system, whose control plane lives inside a single hidden folder. Master that structure, Vellotti contends, and you stop prompting a chatbot and start orchestrating a platform.
article.body:
The .claude/ directory is where the operating-system analogy becomes concrete. It contains five subsystems: CLAUDE.md, a persistent instructions file loaded into every session's system prompt; rules/, for modular path-scoped guidance; skills/, for reusable workflow packages; agents/, for specialized sub-agent personas; and settings.json, which governs permissions — which shell commands are allowed, which are denied. A companion global directory (~/.claude/) holds personal preferences and an auto-memory layer that saves learnings across projects without manual curation. Together they form the runtime environment for AI-assisted work.

The densest section covers *skills* and *hooks*. A skill is a SKILL.md file — a workflow package invokable by slash command — that encodes domain expertise the way a Unix alias encodes a complex command: /make-slides, /review-pr, /deploy-staging. The challenge Vellotti identifies is reliable auto-invocation: getting the model to trigger the right skill without the user typing the exact command. His solution is a hook — a shell script that fires on the UserPromptSubmit lifecycle event, runs a deterministic keyword match against the workspace's skill index, and invokes the matching skill before any inference begins. Hooks intercept 25 lifecycle events, from PreToolUse to Stop; all hook logic runs locally, consuming no API tokens.

**Sub-agents** address a different problem: context window bloat. When Claude Code performs a long research task, every intermediate tool call crowds the primary context window, displacing the working memory that actually matters. Spawning a sub-agent via the built-in Task tool gives that research its own isolated window; the parent session receives only the summary. Vellotti's OS analogy maps cleanly — sub-agents are processes forked from the main thread, with their own stack and a clean return value. Claude Code can run up to roughly ten concurrently.

The tutorial distinguishes three layers of tool connectivity. The *CLI* is the invocation surface — the terminal command, slash commands, piped input. *MCP* (Model Context Protocol), an open standard Anthropic released in late 2024, is the universal adapter: it connects Claude Code to external services — GitHub, databases, Slack, Tavily's real-time web-search API — as structured tool calls the model can invoke natively. The Agent SDK sits at the bottom as the programmatic orchestration layer for teams building custom pipelines. A demonstration skill using **Tavily** shows the pattern in miniature: package the Tavily MCP server as a Claude Code skill, and the model can search the live web from a plain-language phrase without leaving the terminal.

The opening segment maps adjacent products. Cowork is Anthropic's desktop application for non-technical users who want Claude to automate file management and cross-app tasks without writing code. OpenClaw — unaffiliated with Anthropic — is a community-built open-source agent that integrates directly into messaging apps (WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage) and functions more as a personal automation layer than a development tool. Vellotti's framing helps locate Claude Code in this landscape: it is the power-user tier, designed for people who want to extend and orchestrate its behavior rather than simply prompt it.

concepts.definition: Anthropic's agentic coding command-line interface and IDE tool. It reads a codebase, edits files across directories, runs shell commands, manages git, and connects to external services — all from natural-language instructions. Available as a terminal CLI, VS Code and JetBrains plugins, and a standalone desktop app.

Reusable workflow packages stored as SKILL.md files in the .claude/skills/ directory. Each skill encodes domain expertise — a sequence of steps, tool invocations, and instructions — and can be triggered by slash command (e.g. /make-slides) or automatically via hooks. They follow an open Agent Skills standard that works across multiple AI tools.

Event-driven shell scripts that intercept Claude Code lifecycle events — UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, and roughly 25 total. A hook receives context as JSON on stdin, performs arbitrary local logic, and signals Claude Code to proceed (exit 0) or block (exit 2). All logic runs on the local machine and consumes no API tokens.

Isolated Claude Code worker processes spawned by the main session via the Task tool. Each sub-agent has its own context window, tool access, and system prompt; the parent receives only the summary result, keeping the main context window clean. Up to roughly ten can run concurrently, enabling parallel work across long agentic sessions.

The built-in Claude Code mechanism for spawning sub-agents. Calling the Task tool creates an isolated worker with its own context window and tool access; the result returned to the parent is a summary, not the full intermediate transcript. It is the primary mechanism for parallelism and context preservation in long sessions.

An open standard released by Anthropic in late 2024 for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources. MCP servers expose external services — GitHub, databases, Slack, web-search APIs — as structured tool calls the model can invoke natively, functioning as a universal adapter between the model and the broader software ecosystem.

The finite working memory of a large language model — the total amount of text (instructions, conversation history, tool results) that fits in one inference call. When the context window fills, earlier content is displaced. Managing context window usage is a central concern in long agentic tasks.

A configurable bar at the bottom of the Claude Code terminal interface. Any shell script can populate it, receiving session data (current model, cost, context usage, git branch) as JSON on stdin and returning whatever text should be displayed. It runs locally with no API cost.

A real-time web search and content-extraction API designed for AI agents. In Claude Code it is commonly deployed as an MCP server, giving the model native access to live web results from a plain-language prompt. It returns structured data rather than raw HTML, making it practical for agents that need to reason over results.

Anthropic's desktop application aimed at non-technical users who want to automate file management, document editing, and cross-app tasks through a chat interface — without writing code. It productizes behaviors that non-developers had been using Claude Code to achieve.

An open-source personal automation agent, unaffiliated with Anthropic, that integrates into messaging apps — WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage, Slack, Discord — and can act across files, calendar, email, and browser. It targets personal automation rather than software development, with its own community skill marketplace.

The programmatic orchestration layer of Claude Code, used by teams building custom AI pipelines. It provides full control over tool access, permissions, and session orchestration — including HTTP-based hooks that POST JSON to external services — for cases where the CLI alone is insufficient.

In the Claude Code context, the terminal invocation surface: the claude command, slash commands, piped input, and scripting hooks for CI/CD integration. It is the layer at which a human or automation directly issues instructions to Claude Code, as opposed to MCP (which connects external tools) or the Agent SDK (which orchestrates programmatically).

repos.summary: The official Tavily MCP server. It exposes Tavily's web search, URL content extraction, and domain-mapping APIs as structured tool calls that Claude Code — or any MCP-compatible client — can invoke natively. Commonly used to give AI agents reliable access to live web information without building a custom scraper.

Anthropic's curated library of official Agent Skills for Claude Code, covering slide generation, code review, staging deployment, and more. Each skill is a SKILL.md file following the open Agent Skills standard and is installable in any Claude Code workspace via slash command.
